prompt: What does raising the temperature change?
hint: Compare the three tables for `the coffee is`.

choices.text: How evenly the shares are spread among the words
choices.why: Right. The same five words appear at every temperature; at 2 their shares are closer together than at 0.5.

choices.text: Which words the model knows
choices.why: The vocabulary is fixed by training. `sweet` never appears after `coffee is`, at any temperature.

choices.text: The order in which the words are ranked
choices.why: The order was hot, strong, ready, cold, bitter in all three tables.

choices.text: The facts the model learnt from its file during training
choices.why: Temperature is applied after the scores are computed. The model itself is untouched.

prompt: At what point does temperature act?
hint: Think of the steps from scores to a drawn word.

choices.text: During training, when the model's weights are learnt
choices.why: Training is long over by the time you send a prompt. Temperature is a setting per request.

choices.text: After the word is drawn, to decide whether to keep it
choices.why: Nothing is checked after the draw. The shares were already reshaped before it.

choices.text: Before the model reads the prompt
choices.why: The prompt is read first, and the scores come from it. Temperature works on those scores.

choices.text: After the scores, before the draw
choices.why: Yes. Every score is divided by the temperature, then turned into shares, then one word is drawn.

prompt: `toylm dist "the coffee is" --temperature 2` gave `bitter` what percentage?
hint: Read the last line of the third table.

prompt: At temperature 1, `hot` is about 3.2 times as likely as `strong`. What happens to that ratio at temperature 0.5?
hint: The scores are divided by 0.5, which doubles them.

choices.text: It doubles, to about 6.4
choices.why: Doubling the scores doubles the gap, and the ratio grows exponentially with the gap, not in proportion to it.

choices.text: It is squared, to about ten
choices.why: Right: 86.8% against 8.5%. Doubling every score doubles the gap between two of them, and the ratio of the shares is e raised to that gap.

choices.text: It stays at 3.2, since only the overall shape changes
choices.why: The tables show it moving: 86.8 against 8.5 is about ten to one.

choices.text: It halves, to about 1.6
choices.why: That is the direction a higher temperature moves it.

prompt: Why will `toylm` never say `sweet` after `coffee is`, even at a very high temperature?

choices.text: A high temperature only boosts words that were already common in the file
choices.why: It does the opposite: it brings the rare words up towards the common ones.

choices.text: `sweet` has no score there to rescale
choices.why: Right. Temperature reshapes the scores the model gave; a word that never followed `coffee is` has nothing to reshape.

choices.text: `toylm` caps its temperature below the level where new words would appear
choices.why: There is no cap. The command refuses only a negative temperature.

choices.text: `sweet` is not in its vocabulary
choices.why: It is: the file says `the cake is sweet`. It is missing after `coffee is`.

prompt: The raw score a model gives each next token, before it is turned into a share, is called a ___.
hint: The word for the number before the percentages are worked out.

prompt: Two runs of `toylm generate "the coffee is" --temperature 0` with seeds 1 and 2 printed the same thing. Why?

choices.text: Both seeds happened to draw the same word
choices.why: With nothing to draw, there was no luck involved.

choices.text: The seed is ignored by `toylm` entirely
choices.why: At temperature 1 the same seeds gave different sentences, so it is not ignored.

choices.text: The model remembered its answer from the first run
choices.why: Each run starts from nothing. No state is kept between them.

choices.text: At 0 nothing is drawn, so the seed has no work
choices.why: Right. The top word is taken every time; the seed only matters when something is drawn.

prompt: `is the` gives `bread`, `coffee` and `soup` a third each. Why does `toylm` at temperature 0 always pick `bread`?
hint: Look at how ties are broken.

choices.text: Bread is mentioned most often in the corpus
choices.why: The three shares are exactly equal here, so frequency decided nothing.

choices.text: Temperature 0 picks the shortest word when scores are equal
choices.why: Length plays no part. `soup` is as short as `bread` and loses to it.

choices.text: Ties are sorted alphabetically
choices.why: Yes. A rule decides the tie, so the output is still the same every run.

choices.text: It is drawn at random among the three
choices.why: At 0 nothing is drawn. If it were random, the three would take turns.

prompt: You call a hosted model at temperature 0 and two requests return slightly different text. What is the best explanation?
hint: What happens to near-ties on many processors?

choices.text: The API ignored the temperature you sent
choices.why: Not needed to explain it: output at temperature 0 can vary on a hosted model without that, and the provider's documentation says what it guarantees.

choices.text: The model learnt from your first request before answering the second
choices.why: A model does not train on requests while it answers them.

choices.text: Arithmetic differed, and a near-tie flipped
choices.why: Right. Floating-point sums in a different order, a different batch or an updated model can change which token is on top, and the rest follows.

choices.text: Temperature 0 is random by design, like temperature 1
choices.why: At 0 the top token is taken. The variation comes from the machinery, not from a draw.

prompt: Which of these are reasons a hosted model at temperature 0 can still vary between requests? Choose all that apply.
hint: The section lists three, all outside the idea of temperature.

choices.text: Floating-point sums done in a different order
choices.why: Yes. On near-ties the last digit can decide the top token.

choices.text: The request being batched with other requests
choices.why: Yes. How a batch is formed can change the arithmetic.

choices.text: The model behind the name being updated
choices.why: Yes, and that changes everything at once.

choices.text: The temperature being applied after the draw
choices.why: Temperature is applied before the draw, and at 0 there is no draw.

prompt: Your extraction pipeline runs at temperature 0. What does this lesson say your code must still do?
hint: Close to deterministic is not guaranteed.

choices.text: Handle a reply that differs between runs
choices.why: Right. Variation is rare at 0, and the program still has to cope with it.

choices.text: Nothing more: temperature 0 guarantees identical replies from a hosted model
choices.why: That guarantee is what providers do not make.

choices.text: Retry until two replies match exactly
choices.why: Two matching replies can both be wrong; matching is not the test of a good reply.

choices.text: Raise the temperature slightly so the output becomes stable
choices.why: A higher temperature adds variation; it does not remove it.

prompt: At temperature 0 a model gives the same wrong opening hour every run. What does the repetition tell you?
hint: Temperature 0 picks the most likely answer.

choices.text: That it is probably correct, since a guess would vary
choices.why: Stability comes from the rule, not from knowledge, and a rule can repeat a mistake.

choices.text: That the model checked the hour against a source
choices.why: Nothing in the loop checks facts.

choices.text: That the temperature setting was ignored by the provider
choices.why: A repeated answer is exactly what temperature 0 should produce.

choices.text: Only that it is the likeliest answer
choices.why: Right. Repetition shows the model's top choice, and a top choice can be wrong; lesson 5 is about why.

prompt: Which task does this lesson suggest running at temperature 0, or close to it?
hint: One right output, or many good ones?

choices.text: Brainstorming twenty names for a new drink
choices.why: That wants different candidates each run, so a higher temperature.

choices.text: Writing a friendly reply to a customer
choices.why: Ordinary writing starts from the provider's default.

choices.text: Suggesting alternative headlines for an article
choices.why: Alternatives to pick from want variety.

choices.text: Pulling the date and total out of invoices
choices.why: Right. There is one right output, and any variation is an error.

prompt: At 1.5, two of six samples said `eight on sunday` after `the café opens at`. What is wrong with that answer?

choices.text: Nothing; it is a sentence from the file, so it is correct
choices.why: Being in the file makes it fluent and true of Sundays, not the answer to when the café opens.

choices.text: It is not grammatical
choices.why: It is grammatical. The problem is what it says, not how.

choices.text: True on Sundays, wrong for the other days
choices.why: Right. It is a real sentence from the file, drawn where it does not answer the question.

choices.text: `eight` has no score after `opens at`, so it cannot be drawn
choices.why: It has 25% at temperature 1, and 1.5 raises its share.

prompt: Somebody raises the temperature to get more accurate answers. What is wrong with the plan?

choices.text: Nothing: higher temperatures make the model reason more
choices.why: Temperature reshapes scores; it adds no reasoning.

choices.text: Temperature decides how far down the list a draw reaches, not truth
choices.why: Right. A higher temperature draws unlikely continuations more often, and those are wrong more often.

choices.text: Accuracy needs a temperature above 2
choices.why: There is no setting that makes answers truer.

choices.text: Accuracy depends only on the seed
choices.why: The seed decides which draw happens, and often changes the wording. It has nothing to do with truth.

prompt: A prompt can be read two ways, and at temperature 0 you always get the same reading. What has temperature 0 done to the ambiguity?
hint: Where did the other reading go?

choices.text: Hidden it
choices.why: Right. The likeliest reading wins every run and the other never shows. The fix belongs in the prompt.

choices.text: Removed it, because the model settled on the correct reading of the prompt
choices.why: It settled on the likeliest reading, which need not be the one you meant.

choices.text: Nothing at all; ambiguity only exists at a high temperature, where several readings appear
choices.why: The ambiguity is in the prompt at every temperature. A high one only makes it visible.

choices.text: Doubled it
choices.why: The output did not vary, so nothing was doubled.

prompt: Put the steps from the model's scores to a drawn word in order, at a temperature above 0.
hint: Temperature acts between two of them.
items: The model gives every next word a score
Every score is divided by the temperature
The scores are turned into shares that add up to 100%
One word is drawn in proportion to its share

prompt: Match each temperature to what `toylm` did with `the coffee is`.
hint: The tables and runs in this lesson.
